_rules: This file is the definition of done. Sessions may only change the `passes` field.
Set passes=true only after the feature's acceptance test passes. The Stop hook re-runs every passes=true backend test.
Frontend acceptance specs (frontend/tests/acceptance) need the stack running; the session-report skill runs them.
Never edit backend/tests/acceptance/ or frontend/tests/acceptance/. If a test looks wrong, stop and say so.

features.description: FareSimulator(seed) implements both LiveFareProvider and CachedFareProvider; same seed gives identical tickets, different seeds give different prices.

Prices come from a hierarchical model (route level x date effect x weekday x noise), calibrated to the real fares in the spec. Saturdays cost more than Tuesdays on average; a return is cheaper than two one-ways; cached lowest prices are noisy but correlated with true lowest prices (r > 0.8).
exhaustive_best(sim, trip, prefs) searches the full candidate space without a budget and returns the best ScoredItinerary; no budgeted plan can beat it.

run_benchmark(planners, budgets, seeds, trips) returns one record per run with planner, trip, budget, seed, searches_used, best_utility, optimum_utility, regret, wall_ms. BENCHMARK_TRIPS has at least 10 variants of the Lima trip (date windows, flexibility, return vs open-jaw, preference profiles). Deterministic.
`uv run python -m app.bench --planners heuristic --out <dir>` writes bench.json, bench.md (an ablation table with mean regret per planner and budget) and regret.png (regret against search budget).
The planner runs independent searches concurrently: with 50 ms simulated latency per search, a plan takes under half the serial time.

OpenAI replaces Anthropic behind the existing LLM protocol (internal message format unchanged; the adapter converts tools, messages and responses). Models are chosen per role in one place (parse, narrate, baseline) from settings. A SpendGuard refuses LLM calls once recorded spend passes a monthly cap.
unsupported_numbers(text, tool_outputs) returns every money amount or duration in an LLM answer that does not appear in tool outputs (within £1 / 0.1 h). Dates, ranks and small counts are ignored.

Planner 'llm': the LLM chooses searches itself through a raw search tool and the same cached-fare tool the statistical planners get, under the same budget. By default it uses the strongest OpenAI reasoning model (role 'baseline'). run_benchmark accepts planners=['llm'] with an injected llm_factory.
Planner 'voi-gp': Gaussian process over hub x date x structure with a cost-aware acquisition function. Mean regret beats 'heuristic' at budgets 10 and 20.

Planner 'voi-hier': hierarchical Bayesian fare model (route/date/weekday effects, partial pooling) choosing searches by expected utility gain (Thompson sampling or knowledge gradient). Mean regret beats 'heuristic' at budgets 10 and 20.
POST /api/plan returns a plan_id, ranked itineraries and stats; POST /api/rerank re-scores the stored candidates for new preferences with no new searches and within 200 ms.
Every plan records a trace: ordered events (cache_bound, prune, search) with hub, slices, reason and searches_used after each search. One search event per budgeted search.
POST /api/race returns, per planner, the best-so-far utility and regret after each search. mode=replay serves recorded runs instantly; mode=live runs fresh and is rate-limited per client (HTTP 429).

POST /api/preferences/parse turns free text ('I'd pay £150 for a night in Madrid') into a partial Preferences update via the 'parse' model with structured output; values are clamped to valid ranges and unrelated text changes nothing.

POST /api/explain narrates the top options of a plan with the 'narrate' model. Answers go through the grounding check; one retry if any number is unsupported. The response reports retries and the final unsupported count.
Form-first page for the Lima scenario: departure date, flexibility, search budget, preference sliders and a free-text preference box; running a search shows ranked trade-off cards.
Moving a preference slider reorders the cards via /api/rerank only (no new /api/plan call).
Race panel animates the recorded race (one regret line per planner) with a 'race it live' button; trace panel lists prune and search events.
/how-it-works page with sections Architecture, Fare models, Benchmark (rendering the current ablation table and regret chart from reports/latest).

Pairwise 'would you rather' questions chosen for information gain update a posterior over preference weights (Bradley-Terry likelihood). Simulated users with known weights: after 5 answers, the top itinerary under the posterior mean matches the one under their true weights for at least 80% of users.

Backend Dockerfile (uv, non-root) and fly.toml (internal_port 8000, scale to zero); frontend deploys to Vercel with BACKEND_URL; /api/health reports version, fare source and whether the spend cap is reached.
